articles.title: Karnataka High Court quashes RGUHS Syndicate’s resolution to exclude Senate members from panels for inspection of existing affiliated colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The High Court of Karnataka ruled that members of the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) Senate cannot be excluded from Local Inspection Committees (LICs) for inspecting nursing and allied health sciences colleges. The court also stated that any amendments to or repeals of the RGUHS statute must be submitted by the Syndicate to the Senate, which alone has the power to approve them before submission to the state government.  The court dismissed a petition from the Karnataka State Association of the Management of Nursing and Allied Health Science Institutions, upholding the Senate's authority in LIC membership for affiliation decisions.

articles.title: Telangana IT Minister for stronger digital push in govt. schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries, visited a 'Super Summer Camp' in Manthani town to support the development of digital infrastructure in government schools. The camp, organized by T-Fiber and Super Teacher Edu Reforms Pvt. Ltd. aims to bridge the digital divide and provide hands-on learning experiences in computer education, AI, and robotics for students. Similar camps will be held in Peddapalli, Ramagundam, and Sulthanabad until May 23rd with a closing ceremony scheduled for May 26th.

articles.title: Summer coaching camps begin across Vizag district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The District Sports Authority of Visakhapatnam launched 65 annual summer coaching camps across 28 sports disciplines in rural and urban centers, running until May 31. The initiative, organized by the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP), aims to introduce children aged 8-16 to structured training and promote a healthy lifestyle through regular sporting activity.  District Sports Development Officer June Gallyot emphasized the camps' importance in identifying talent, encouraging constructive summer use, and instilling discipline from a young age. The camps are being conducted across multiple centers with support from the Department of Ayush, providing necessary equipment and emergency medical support through nearby Primary Health Centres.

articles.title: Buddha Purnima marked at Buddhavanam with ‘Mobile Museum on Wheels’ launch - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Tourism and Culture Minister Jupally Krishna Rao attended the 2570th Buddha Purnima celebrations at Buddhavanam, where traditional Buddhist rituals were performed.  The event included the inauguration of a children's play area and the launch of a "Mobile Museum on Wheels" initiative to promote Buddhist heritage education across Telangana. The mobile unit features replicas of Buddhist sculptures, educational materials, and digital content, aiming to foster understanding of Buddhist thought and values among younger generations.

articles.title: Ofsted inspections pushing headteachers to ‘point of destruction’, union chief says | Teaching | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), criticized Ofsted, England's schools watchdog, for pressuring educators to the point of destruction.  Whiteman addressed the union's annual conference in Belfast after a high court dismissal of a legal challenge against Ofsted's new inspection framework and subsequent discussions with the Department for Education (DfE). The NAHT leader called for greater safeguards against potential harm from the system, while also praising recent government policies on free school meals and family hubs. Whiteman emphasized the role teachers play in challenging societal divisions and promoting respect for educators.

articles.title: Changing lives: Virginia students repair old cars and donate them to single mothers | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Louisa County High School in Mineral, Virginia, partners with Giving Words, a nonprofit organization founded by Eddie Brown, to provide automotive technology students with hands-on experience repairing donated vehicles. The program gives single mothers access to reliable transportation while teaching students valuable skills and fostering a sense of purpose.  The initiative involves students performing essential repairs on donated cars, ensuring they meet safety standards before being given away.

articles.title: KEERA to be established for structural reforms in engineering education: Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has decided to establish the Karnataka Engineering Education Reform Authority (KEERA), following recommendations from an Expert Committee on Reforms in Technical Education. The committee, led by former director of IIIT-B, S. Sadagopan, proposed structural reforms for engineering education.  The government plans to bring separate legislation to establish KEERA and will discuss the matter soon.

articles.title: Cambridge confirms AS-level math exam leak, says working on determining next steps - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) confirmed that its AS-level mathematics paper was shared prematurely, violating regulations. This incident follows reports of a leak and concerns about exam transparency from parents and students. CIE is investigating the extent of the leak and will provide an update on May 7th. The organization emphasizes its commitment to protecting the integrity of exams and ensuring student fairness.

articles.title: Gujarat High Court, after attire remarks in court, asks IIT Gandhinagar to ‘show sympathy’ to suspended student - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat High Court orally advised the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IIT-Gn) to show sympathy towards a postgraduate student who was previously reprimanded for her attire. The court acknowledged the student's age and potential lack of understanding of consequences, stating that her conduct did not warrant suspension despite initial concerns about decorum in court.  The court emphasized that past actions played a role in its decision.

articles.title: Sindh education department to introduce religious textbooks for Hindu students - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh Education and Literacy Department plans to introduce religious textbooks for Hindu students in grades three to five across government schools. The department requested the Sindh Textbook Board (STBB) to distribute these books, with the cost of publication covered by Prem Sagar Sanstha Karachi. This follows a similar move by the federal government in 2023, where the National Curriculum Council (NCC) issued no-objection certificates for publishing religious books for minority students.

articles.title: Cambridge A-level paper leak brings distress to bright students - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Following reports of an alleged A-level paper leak, the Inter-Board of Coordination Commission (IBCC) has requested a report from Cambridge to investigate.  The IBCC's Executive Director, Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah, stated that they will take "every possible step" for students after receiving the report. Parents and teachers expressed outrage over the alleged leak, with some questioning the integrity of the exam system. A Cambridge spokesperson confirmed their awareness of the reports and pledged to investigate thoroughly.

articles.title: PMDC announces closure of admissions for academic session 2025–2026 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has closed admissions for the 2025-2026 academic year, with no exceptions allowed after April 15th.  PMDC stated that any admissions granted beyond the deadline will be invalid and violate regulations. The council also urged institutions to comply with these regulations to maintain transparency in medical and dental education. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) has criticized the decision, arguing that vacant seats are due to high fees, not a lack of qualified candidates.

articles.title: NMC does away with ceiling on MBBS intake - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has revised its regulations for undergraduate medical education, removing restrictions on the number of MBBS seats a college can offer and the maximum distance between a college and its affiliated hospital. The changes allow colleges to increase their intake without limitations and adjust distances based on location. These modifications aim to provide greater flexibility in establishing new medical colleges across India.

articles.title: Office for Students’ University of Sussex humiliation is a symptom of deeper failings | Office for Students | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Office for Students (OfS) faced a setback this week when the high court rejected its attempt to fine the University of Sussex over Kathleen Stock's tenure. The ruling highlighted the OfS's failures in its regulatory efforts, including bias and jurisdictional issues.  Susan Lapworth, former chief executive, initiated the investigation in 2021, but despite years of effort, the OfS has yet to demonstrate significant progress for students. This failure contrasts with the growing financial turmoil within the higher education sector, where institutions are facing closures and redundancies. The new leadership under Ruth Hannant and Polly Payne faces a challenging task in restoring trust and effectively regulating the sector.

articles.title: Amid furore on social media, Cambridge says 'aware' of reports about question paper leak - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) acknowledged reports of a leaked AS mathematics question paper in Pakistan, stating they are investigating the matter thoroughly.  The CIE, part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, offers internationally recognized exams to over scores of schools globally. The organization previously addressed leaks in 2025 and 2024, offering resits for affected candidates. CIE exams are typically held twice a year, with results released in August and January.

articles.title: SRM-AP launches AI-integrated PG programmes in Economics, Psychology - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ch. Satish Kumar, Vice-Chancellor of SRM University-AP, highlighted the importance of integrating domain knowledge with emerging technologies in postgraduate education.  At the launch of AI-integrated M.Sc. Economics and M.Sc. Psychology programs by Easwari School of Liberal Arts (ESLA), he emphasized that students must be equipped to apply AI tools for analysis, prediction, and decision-making. This integration prepares students for real-world challenges and future uncertainties.

articles.title: Meet Dattatreya Ramchandra Kaprekar: The Indian mathematician who discovered a ‘ghost number’ that always returns to itself | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dattatreya Ramchandra Kaprekar, a schoolteacher, discovered the Kaprekar constant, a number that repeatedly converges to 6174 when applied to any four-digit number with different digits.  His work gained international attention after mathematician Martin Gardner publicized it in Scientific American.  The Kaprekar constant is now used as a teaching tool for its simplicity and relevance to computer science concepts like iteration and recursion.

articles.title: Lost copy of seventh-century poem in Old English discovered at Rome library | Poetry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Trinity College Dublin scholars discovered a lost copy of Caedmon’s Hymn, the earliest surviving poem in the English language, at the National Central Library of Rome. The manuscript, believed to have been transcribed by a monk between AD800 and AD830, is significant because it contains the Old English version in the main body of the text, reflecting the growing status of the language in the ninth century.  The discovery was made possible through digitization efforts by the Rome library, which has made the manuscript available online for research purposes.

articles.title: What you need to know about Karnataka’s Rohith Vemula Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government approved the revised Karnataka Rohith Vemula (Prevention of Discrimination, Exclusion or Injustice) (Right to Education and Dignity) Bill, 2026, after months of discussions. The bill aims to protect the rights of students, faculty, and staff from scheduled castes and tribes by guaranteeing equal access to education in all higher educational institutions across the state.

articles.title: Teaching in classes grouped by ability does not hamper progress of less able pupils, study finds | Schools | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new study by University College London’s Institute of Education found that setting students by ability does not significantly harm the attainment of low-prior-attaining or socioeconomically disadvantaged pupils.  The research, backed by the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF), showed that high-achieving students in mixed-ability classes made two months less progress on average compared to those in schools using setting. However, the study also found that mixed-ability classrooms did not negatively impact low-prior-attaining pupils and provided some benefits for high-achievers.  The findings suggest that school leaders should consider setting based on individual needs rather than solely by ability.

articles.title: ‘Culture of misogyny’: teacher surrounded by hundreds of students and pelted with food at elite Brisbane boys’ school, court told | Australian education | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria Sparrow, a teacher at Marist College Ashgrove, is suing the school for alleged misogyny and assault after being surrounded by hundreds of male students who pelted her with food. Gerard Forde, Sparrow's barrister, argued that the school allowed a culture of misogyny to develop and exist, citing multiple complaints from female staff members about their treatment.  Forde also presented evidence of other incidents involving sexist behavior towards teachers, including online harassment and threats against a teacher and his family. The case is scheduled for further hearings in the Brisbane Supreme Court.

articles.title: Bengaluru to host pan-India IIT summit on May 16 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Government of Karnataka, in partnership with the Pan-IIT Alumni India Association, will host the Pan-IIT Bangalore Summit 2026 on May 16th. The conference, themed around "Technology Sovereignty," aims to bring together 2,000 participants from across 23 IITs and other stakeholders like policy makers, technology leaders, startup founders, and investors.  The summit will feature high-level plenaries, panels, and tracks on AI, defense, semiconductors, energy, mobility, and healthcare, as well as a pitch-a-thon for startups and a hackathon to tackle real-world challenges. The event is intended to foster collaboration between academia, industry, and government to drive India's technological advancement.

articles.title: Half of England’s schools unfit due to leaks, mould and faulty toilets, poll finds | Schools | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Half of headteachers surveyed by the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) reported that parts of their schools are either unusable or unfit for purpose due to issues such as leaks, damp, mold, asbestos, and aging infrastructure.  Almost three-quarters of respondents said their school's toilet blocks were either closed or not fit for purpose, with almost two-fifths reporting similar problems with facilities reserved for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). The NAHT is calling on the government to fully fund essential capital expenditure across all state schools in England.  A Department for Education spokesperson stated that the government is committed to addressing the legacy of neglect in school buildings, including removing Raac and providing long-term investment to improve their condition.

articles.title: Government signs MoU with State Legal Services Authority to promote legal awareness and child protection in schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government and Telangana State Legal Services Authority (TSLSA) signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen legal literacy and child protection in schools. The initiative, implemented across 5,711 high schools, will include legal awareness sessions for students and teachers, awareness campaigns on child rights, and the establishment of legal literacy and child rights clubs.  The program also includes training for teachers, provision of legal aid and counselling services, and efforts to support school dropouts. The MoU is in effect for two years with a potential extension.

articles.title: ‘Civil service exam tests emotional fortitude rather than intellectual capability’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Benjo P. Jose, a 2024 batch IAS officer, advised civil service aspirants to avoid blindly following strategies and instead focus on their individual needs during the exam preparation process. He emphasized the importance of emotional resilience and encouraged aspiring civil servants to cultivate diverse interests beyond just the UPSC examination. Fabi Rasheed, another 2024 batch IAS officer, stressed the need for a clear understanding of personal motivations for joining the civil service.  Sylesh Fernandes, an exam mentor, urged students to prioritize core subjects like Indian polity and maintain consistent study schedules.

articles.title: Govt. may establish labs in varsities to train students for space sector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister Jitendra Singh reviewed plans to establish seven space laboratories in universities and colleges across India, aiming to build a skilled workforce for the expanding space sector. The initiative is part of efforts to attract private investment and support the growth of India's burgeoning private space ecosystem, which has seen over 400 startups emerge since 2019.  The government has launched programs like the Technology Adoption Fund to facilitate commercialization of innovations and train individuals in specialized areas related to space technology.

articles.title: Provide fixed fund of at least ₹1 crore for academic chairs in universities: Prof. Baraguru Committee to government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A committee headed by writer Baraguru Ramachandrappa has recommended that the State government provide a fixed sum of at least ₹1 crore for each academic chair established in universities. The committee also suggested mandatory financial allocations upon chair establishment and regular reporting on their activities to ensure equal funding and eliminate discrimination.  The report further recommends that chairs should be named after individuals with significant cultural contributions and focus on regional problems, becoming centers of knowledge creation.

articles.title: Warangal: Over 1,300 SRU students secure jobs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SR University hosted its 'Placement Success Meet-2026' on Saturday, showcasing strong placement outcomes for the current academic year.  Associate Director (Training & Placements) G. Sunil Reddy reported over 1,300 students secured jobs in leading companies, with more opportunities expected as recruitment processes continue. Chancellor A. Varada Reddy attributed the success to disciplined preparation and institutional support.

articles.title: BITS Pilani opens smart manufacturing centre in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BITS Pilani has opened its Smart Manufacturing Competency Centre (SMCC) in Bengaluru's Electronic City. The centre, designed to foster industry-academia collaboration, will offer short and long-term training programs for industries such as aerospace, defense, electronics, automotive, and advanced manufacturing. BITS Pilani representatives believe the SMCC can act as a problem-solving and innovation partner for these sectors.

articles.title: ‘Maintain consistency’: toppers offer tips to Civil Service aspirants - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Civil Service Gateway 2026, a two-day event held at the Jimmy George Indoor Stadium, brought together civil service toppers to share their experiences and advice with aspiring candidates.  Participants like Meera K. and Sreeja J.S. emphasized the importance of consistent preparation, setting boundaries for topics, and utilizing resources like The Hindu for current affairs. Others, such as Anjana B. and Divya S. highlighted the significance of mental health and overcoming obstacles during their journeys to success.  Mohamed Shezin C.P. shared his remarkable story of balancing work and studies while achieving a high rank despite facing Cerebral Palsy. The summit was presented by Fortune IAS Academy, with support from SBI and Civils 360 IAS Academy.

articles.title: Param Science Experience Centre inaugurated in Whitefield - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Param Science Experience Centre (ParSEC), a 30,000 sq. ft facility in Whitefield, opened to the public on Sunday.  The Param Foundation initiative aims to shift science education from rote memorization to experiential learning. The centre features galleries covering artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, light and optics, electromagnetism, design thinking, and ancient Indian scientific knowledge systems. Former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the facility, while Kris Gopalakrishnan, co-founder of Infosys, emphasized the importance of science for human progress and economic growth.

articles.title: Medical Education Department keen on 15% NRI quota in all government medical colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Medical Education Department, Karnataka, plans to reserve 15% of all seats in its 24 government medical colleges for NRIs starting in the academic year 2026-27. This move aims to make these colleges self-sufficient and reduce reliance on state grants. The department will submit a proposal to the government soon, with the final decision expected to be made by the Cabinet.  Private colleges currently charge around ₹40 lakh to ₹47 lakh per annum for NRI quota seats, while the government has set a fee of ₹25 lakh per annum for NRI quota seats in 2025-26.

articles.title: International seminar to commemorate Prof. K.N. Panikkar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sreenarayana Guru Open University (SGOU) and the Kerala History Congress are hosting a two-day international seminar to honor the late Prof. K.N. Panikkar's contributions to history. The event, themed "Cultural Logics of Nationalism: Hegemony and Democratic Struggles," will be held on April 28th and 29th at the SGOU academic block. Former Minister M.A. Baby will inaugurate the seminar, while Prof Jagathy Raj V.P. will preside over the session.  Distinguished historians from premier Indian universities will participate in paper presentations and discussions.

articles.title: GT Tech partners with BotClub to strengthen science education - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gram Tarang Technologies Private Limited (GT Tech) and BotClub Private Limited, an education technology start-up, announced a strategic partnership to enhance science education in schools. The collaboration will utilize BotClub’s “A-One” classroom system, which integrates digital visuals with physical models and provides analytics on student learning outcomes, according to D.N. Rao, Vice-President of Centurion University and GT Tech promoter.

articles.title: 859 students get admissions on first day of KL University counselling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KL University Vice-Chancellor G. Parthasarathy Verma reported that 859 students were admitted on the first day of counseling for engineering, degree, and postgraduate courses at the Vijayawada and Hyderabad campuses. The admissions were based on merit criteria including top ranks in the KLUEEE, scores of 970 marks in Intermediate, and a percentile above 95 in JEE Mains.

articles.title: Use knowledge for progress, be job creators: Vice-President to youth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan urged Rajasthan University graduates to use their knowledge for societal progress and become job creators and nation builders during the university's 35th convocation ceremony.  He emphasized that education should be applied for the betterment of society, innovation, and ethical conduct. The event was attended by Chancellor and Governor Haribhau Bagade.

articles.title: SSLC results: Yadgir records 91.89 pass percentage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yadgir district has achieved a pass percentage of 91.89%, a significant increase from last year's 62.1%. This improvement, attributed to guidance and support from elected representatives, the district administration, and the zilla panchayat, propelled the district to 31st place in the state ranking table. Despite teacher vacancies, the department utilized available teachers effectively through special classes, overnight sessions, preparatory exams, and group discussions.  The efforts of all stakeholders resulted in a substantial improvement in pass percentage across all years, with girls consistently outperforming boys.

articles.title: Evolution of information centres in modern era highlighted at VIT-A.P. University - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalpakkam Saibaba, a former scientist from the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Energy (IGCAR), spoke at World Book and Copyright Day celebrations organized by VIT-A.P. University.  He discussed the evolution of information centers in the modern era and emphasized the importance of research in nation-building. Saibaba encouraged young minds to utilize educational opportunities provided by institutions and government initiatives for societal betterment.

articles.title: SSLC: Belagavi division tops Karnataka with 95.71 pass percentage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Belagavi division, comprising nine educational districts, achieved a pass percentage of 95.71 in the SSLC examination, surpassing all other divisions in the state.  Ishwar Ullagaddi, Additional Commissioner of School Education and Literacy, attributed the success to the 'Mission-40' initiative and targeted academic programs. Two students from the division, Prarthana Nagappa Biradar Patil and Soujanya Basavaraj Kandkur, emerged as State toppers with scores of 625 out of 625.  The overall pass percentage in the division has seen a considerable increase compared to the previous year.

articles.title: Six gold medals to be awarded at BASE convocation on April 27 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar School of Economics (BASE) University in Bengaluru awarded six students with gold medals at its second annual convocation on April 27th.  The six students, including five female students, earned their degrees in economics and financial economics. BASE University will also be presenting 17 rank certificates and 171 degree certificates for the academic years 2023-24 and 2024-25.

articles.title: FYUGP students in Calicut varsity allowed do internship in their own colleges this year - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P. Raveendran, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calicut, has issued an order allowing students in four-year undergraduate programs to complete their internships at their respective colleges this year. This change comes amidst complaints about limited internship opportunities and financial exploitation, as well as difficulties faced by students traveling for internships during the summer months. The new policy allows students to complete their 60 hours of internship within their college environment, with teachers overseeing the work and evaluating performance.

articles.title: APPGECET to be held from April 28 to 30 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) has prepared for the APPGECET-2026, scheduled to be held from April 28th to 30th across the state. The exam will be conducted in a Computer-Based Test (CBT) format with two sessions, from 9 a.m. to 11 noon and 2 p.m. to 4 p.m., at 26 examination centers in 18 towns.  Candidates must arrive early, adhere to instructions, and bring only their hall ticket, application form, valid ID, and ballpoint pen. Electronic gadgets are prohibited.

articles.title: SFI seeks action against faculty members accused of harassing medical PG students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) announced a protest outside the Principal's chamber at Government Medical College, Kozhikode, on April 27th if no action is taken against two faculty members accused of mental harassment towards postgraduate doctors. The SFI claims that all 12 PG doctors have lodged complaints with the Principal, K.P. Sidharth, and the Kerala Medical Post Graduate Association has also demanded action.  The college authorities claim they forwarded the complaint to the internal grievance cell for further action, which will be sent to the Directorate of Medical Education (DME).

articles.title: Jadavpur University got global acclaim despite fiscal crunch: Teachers’ body on PM’s critical remark - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized Jadavpur University in West Bengal, calling it a symbol of anarchy under the TMC's rule.  However, the Jadavpur University Teachers' Association (JUTA) refuted these claims, stating that the university has been recognized globally as a center of excellence despite financial constraints and played a significant role in social justice. JUTA also accused the government of neglecting the university's funding needs and undermining public institutions while supporting private ones.

articles.title: VIT-A.P. University hosts conference on mechanical engineering and materials science - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anjan Kumar Panda, Principal Consultant at Infosys Limited's Turbo Machinery and Plant Engineering, emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary knowledge in modern technology development.  At the fourth International Conference on Advances in Mechanical Engineering and Material Science (ICAMEMS 2026), he highlighted the role of mechanical engineering and materials science in driving innovation in aerospace, robotics, and quantum computing. J. Suryanarayana, Professor at IIT Hyderabad, discussed cryogenic technology's application in resolving heat transfer issues in quantum computing.  P. Arul Mozhivarman, Vice-Chancellor of VIT-A.P., Amaravati, stressed the significance of these fields in robotics, automation, and healthcare innovation.

articles.title: SRM University-A.P. celebrates 10th edition of Research Day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SRM University-AP hosted its tenth Research Day, featuring presentations and collaborations across disciplines. S.S.V. Ramakumar, chief technology officer and executive vice-president of AM Green, spoke on energy transition from an Indian perspective, emphasizing the Princeton Wedge Approach to climate change mitigation.  The event took place on Friday at the university's campus in Guntur district.

articles.title: SRM University-A.P. celebrates 10th edition of Research Day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SRM University-AP celebrated its tenth Research Day, featuring presentations from scholars across disciplines. S.S.V. Ramakumar, chief technology officer and executive vice-president of AM Green, delivered a keynote address on energy transition in India, emphasizing the Princeton Wedge Approach to addressing climate change through incremental solutions.  The event highlighted global trends such as rising gas demand, expanding solar and wind energy, and the shift towards advanced biofuels.

articles.title: OU, Cyient Foundation to collaborate for Industry 4.0 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Osmania University and Cyient Foundation officials met to discuss a strategic collaboration aimed at creating an Industry 4.0-ready workforce. The partnership will focus on establishing skill academies, internships, research centers, and entrepreneurship initiatives to bridge the gap between academia and industry.  The goal is to make Osmania University a hub for innovation and ensure graduates are equipped with the skills needed for a global workforce.

articles.title: NHRC issues notices to Centre, States over poor adoption of NCERT, SCERT textbooks in private schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued notices to the Centre and States seeking explanations regarding inspections or audits into allegations that private schools are substituting government-prescribed textbooks with those from private publishers. The complaint alleges this practice burdens families financially, prompting the NHRC's inquiry.

articles.title: Anagha from Tirthahalli is second topper in SSLC exam-1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anagha K.S. of Vagdevi School in Tirthahalli achieved the second-highest score (624/625) in the SSLC examination, while Kruthi P.S. of Priyadarshini High School secured the third rank with a score of 623/625.  The district of Shivamogga recorded a pass percentage of 96.56%, placing it ninth in the state and marking an improvement from last year's fifth position. The students, who achieved high marks, expressed gratitude for their teachers and parents' support.
